sources.title: Market Liquidity and Funding Liquidity
sources.authors: Markus K. Brunnermeier; Lasse Heje Pedersen
sources.claim: Market liquidity and funding liquidity can reinforce each other, producing destabilizing liquidity spirals and sharp increases in volatility.

sources.title: Modeling and Forecasting Realized Volatility
sources.authors: Torben G. Andersen; Tim Bollerslev; Francis X. Diebold; Paul Labys
sources.claim: High-frequency realized volatility contains persistent information useful for forecasting future volatility and return distributions.

sources.title: Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects
sources.claim: Unexpected increases in market illiquidity are associated with contemporaneously lower returns, while expected illiquidity commands a return premium.

sources.title: Order Flow and Exchange Rate Dynamics
sources.authors: Martin D. D. Evans; Richard K. Lyons
sources.claim: Signed order flow contains substantial information about price changes because trades aggregate dispersed information.

sources.title: Measuring the Information Content of Stock Trades
sources.claim: Trade innovations have persistent price impact; larger trades and wider-spread conditions are associated with larger information effects.

sources.title: Bid, ask and transaction prices in a specialist market with heterogeneously informed traders
sources.authors: Lawrence R. Glosten; Paul R. Milgrom
sources.claim: Adverse selection creates bid-ask spreads and makes observed transaction prices differ from realizable prices.

sources.title: A New Interpretation of Information Rate
sources.claim: Under known probabilities and odds, capital growth is maximized by sizing exposure according to edge rather than using fixed stakes.

sources.title: Foundations of Technical Analysis: Computational Algorithms, Statistical Inference, and Empirical Implementation
sources.authors: Andrew W. Lo; Harry Mamaysky; Jiang Wang
sources.claim: Some technical price patterns can be formalized computationally and may contain incremental information, but statistical validation is essential.

sources.title: Currency momentum strategies
sources.authors: Lukas Menkhoff; Lucio Sarno; Maik Schmeling; Andreas Schrimpf
sources.claim: Cross-sectional currency momentum is significant but partly eroded by transaction costs and constrained by limits to arbitrage.

rules.hypothesis: Very high realized volatility combined with a volume shock may mark a liquidity-stress state in which directional signals deserve less trust.
rules.mechanism: Funding-liquidity and market-liquidity feedback can amplify price moves.
rules.formalization_note: Crypto proxy using realized volatility and relative volume; not a direct rule from the paper.

rules.hypothesis: An extreme realized-volatility state is likely to persist enough to warrant lower conviction and exposure.
rules.formalization_note: Threshold is VERITAS-specific and requires out-of-sample validation.

rules.hypothesis: Strong signed aggressive-buy flow during elevated activity may contain short-horizon positive price information.
rules.formalization_note: Crypto taker-buy share is a proxy; low prior until validated.

rules.hypothesis: Strong signed aggressive-sell flow during elevated activity may contain short-horizon negative price information.
rules.formalization_note: Crypto taker-buy share is a proxy; low prior until validated.

rules.hypothesis: Large aggressive-buy imbalance under high activity may have persistent short-horizon price impact.
rules.mechanism: Information-bearing trades can have persistent price impact.
rules.formalization_note: VERITAS proxy adaptation; trade size and spread are not yet directly observed.

rules.hypothesis: Large aggressive-sell imbalance under high activity may have persistent short-horizon price impact.
rules.mechanism: Information-bearing trades can have persistent price impact.
rules.formalization_note: VERITAS proxy adaptation; trade size and spread are not yet directly observed.

rules.hypothesis: When cross-venue prices diverge materially, executable price uncertainty and adverse-selection risk justify lower confidence.
rules.formalization_note: Cross-exchange divergence is a VERITAS proxy for execution-quality uncertainty.

rules.hypothesis: Position size must be tied to estimated edge and uncertainty, with fractional sizing preferred when probabilities are estimated rather than known.
rules.mechanism: Log-growth optimal sizing under probabilistic edge.
rules.formalization_note: Governance only; no live Kelly sizing until calibration quality is independently established.

rules.hypothesis: Technical patterns must be encoded objectively and validated statistically before promotion.
rules.mechanism: Formal pattern recognition plus statistical inference.
rules.formalization_note: Governance rule for future pattern-library expansion.

rules.hypothesis: Add direct liquidity and price-impact measures before treating volume alone as a complete liquidity proxy.
rules.formalization_note: Research agenda until spread/depth/impact data are wired.

rules.hypothesis: Momentum evidence from another highly liquid 24-hour asset class modestly raises the prior for medium-horizon continuation.
rules.mechanism: Underreaction / delayed overreaction with limits to arbitrage.
rules.formalization_note: Cross-asset analogy only; deliberately low prior for crypto.

rules.hypothesis: Momentum evidence from another highly liquid 24-hour asset class modestly raises the prior for medium-horizon downside continuation.
rules.mechanism: Underreaction / delayed overreaction with limits to arbitrage.
rules.formalization_note: Cross-asset analogy only; deliberately low prior for crypto.
